# PR #3880: Patch (part 1 of 2): your own unit's greyed switch says why, and a unit with no action left says so when tapped

Closes #3821

## What changed

Your own unit now says why it can't switch position, and tapping a unit with no action left shows "that unit has already acted this turn" instead of doing nothing.

**Engine.** `UnitView` has a new optional field, `switchReason`, set only on the viewer's own units.
- **When it is set:** in its controller's main phase with no prompt open, whether or not the unit `canAct`.
- **What it holds:** the refusal `combat::why_cannot_switch_in(…, position_after_switch, true)` gives: Dormant, Frozen, already acted this turn, or can't be in Defense Position (Can't Defend, Indestructible, Evasive, or Warp Disruptor's aura).
- **Why it can't disagree with the list:** `reduce::can_switch` offers a `switchPosition` by the same call, so the field is absent exactly when that switch is offered.
- **Hashes:** `golden::view_texts` strips the key, so `HOTSEAT_HASH` and stored traces don't move.

**jackioh-shared.** `LiveCard`, `InPlay` and `FaceModel` carry the field. `InPlay` drops it when it is word for word the attack reason (a Frozen unit's is both), so the inspect notes say it once.

**Web:**
- **Tap:** `actions.ts` `onClickTarget` shows `attackReason ?? switchReason` as the notice and sends nothing.
- **Switch button:** the greyed switch's `aria-label` and `title` read "Switch position: <reason>". It stays `disabled`.
- **Inspect notes:** `StateNotes.tsx` gets a `switchReason` line.

**Spec and docs:**
- Ruling `R3821000.md`, with its paragraph in `spec/pending/3821.md`.
- One sentence added to `R849000.md`.
- The §10.8 `UnitView` paragraph and one sentence in §4.1.
- A bullet in SURFACE §17.
- The four regenerated wire types: `UnitView`, `LiveCard`, `InPlay`, `FaceModel`.

## Where I departed from the plan (look at this twice)

**`Card.tsx`'s click gate.** The plan only changed `onClickTarget`, but that alone would not have worked. `Card`'s `fire` drops any click on a card the highlight doesn't list (only R979000's `playReason` got through), and a spent unit lists nothing, so its tap never reached `onClickTarget`.

I added `explainsUnit`: a card in a unit zone whose unit has a `switchReason` or `attackReason`. Its click now goes through, but it is **not** stopped there, so it still reaches the zone underneath. Without that, a tap on a spent unit during a Stack or Equip play onto its zone would be swallowed. While a play or an attack is being built, the card's own click changes nothing (`onClickTarget` returns the same interaction).

I limited it to unit-zone cards because the backrow path already turns a backrow card's click into a zone click (R446). Letting those through too could send the same action twice.

Both halves have their own test in `switchReason.test.tsx`. I checked that each test fails when its half is reverted.

## Decisions the issue didn't settle

- **When the field is set.** It is not tied to `canAct`, as the issue first proposed: that rule gives a spent unit no reason, which contradicts the issue's own acceptance criterion. Recorded in the ruling's "Rejected".
- **Which reason a tap shows.** The attack reason still comes first. A unit that may attack but has no target shows its switch reason; the alternative was the client judging which reason applies, which breaks rule 7.
- **The greyed switch stays disabled.** Making it pressable, as R3768000 did for Activate and Trade, is left to part 2. The tap on the card now says the reason.
- **Left alone:**
  - The card's own hover tooltip (`cardTitle`) still shows only `attackReason`. Adding `switchReason` would show "can't be in Defense Position" on every Can't Defend unit all turn.
  - Units held by a carrier or standing in the backrow get no tap notice. That is the same scope as R849000, which only reads `view.you.units`.

# #3821: Patch (part 1 of 2): your own unit's greyed switch says why, and a unit with no action left says so when tapped
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Your own unit's small switch-position button greys out for lots of reasons: the unit can't defend, it is indestructible or evasive, an aura bars Defense Position, or it has already acted this turn. Today nothing ever says which. The greyed button can't be hovered or tapped, and tapping a unit that has already attacked does nothing at all. A unit that can't attack yet does explain itself when tapped. Once this is built, a unit's details say why it can't switch ("this unit can't be in Defense Position"), and tapping a unit with nothing left to do shows "that unit has already acted this turn" in the same place.

## Why

- `apps/web/src/game/Card.tsx:736-770`: `SwitchButton` is `disabled={!legal}` with only `title="Switch position"`. `apps/web/src/game/board.css:1884-1894` gives a disabled switch `pointer-events: none` and opacity 0.35, so even that title never shows.
- `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts:1004-1007`: a tap on your own unit with no listed attack shows only `UnitView.attackReason`. `crates/engine/src/view_for.rs:905-918` (`attack_reason_of`) sends it only while the unit may act, so a spent unit gets none and its tap is silent. The words "No action left this turn" exist only in the Zz badge's `title` and a screen-reader span (`Card.tsx:611-616`), and the badge itself has `pointer-events: none` (`spent.css:32`).
- The engine already has the words: `combat::why_cannot_switch_in` (`crates/engine/src/combat.rs:323-360`) covers Dormant, Frozen, "that unit has already acted this turn" and the Defense bar (Can't Defend R2657000, Indestructible R2179000, Evasive R3543002, Warp Disruptor's aura R1849006).
- About 95 Can't Defend and 42 Indestructible catalog entries (survey count): the greyed switch is everyday. R849000 gave attacks their reason, and #3768 is doing Activate and Trade; the switch is the one own-unit control left silent.

## Proposal

1. Engine: `UnitView.switchReason`, on the viewer's own units only and gated as `attack_reason_of` is. It holds the message of `why_cannot_switch_in` for the unit's own switch (to the other position, spending its exertion), and `None` when that switch is legal. Adding a view field takes a ruling in the issue's block (as R849000 did), with its paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`, the §10.8 view row and `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md`.
2. Client: a tap on your own unit with no attack listed and no `attackReason` shows `switchReason` as its notice and sends nothing, so a spent unit says it has already acted. The unit's inspect notes (`cards/inspect/StateNotes.tsx`) and the switch's accessible name carry the reason. The words are the engine's; the client restates no rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands

`crates/engine/src/view_for.rs` and the view type (the generated `apps/web/src/wire/`), `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`, `Card.tsx`, `apps/web/src/cards/inspect/StateNotes.tsx`; SPEC §4.1, §10.8; a ruling note; SURFACE.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An engine view test: an own Indestructible or Can't Defend unit in Attack Position on its controller's turn carries the Defense refusal; an own unit that has attacked carries "that unit has already acted this turn"; an enemy unit, the opponent's turn and a unit free to switch carry none.
- [ ] A vitest test: `onClickTarget` on an own spent unit returns that notice and no action; on an own unit that may attack it still starts the attack.
- [ ] A vitest test: the unit's inspect notes show the reason.
- [ ] The ruling's proving test is named after it and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes; the regenerated wire types are committed.

## Size and risks

Small to medium: about 8 files across the engine and the web, which makes it hard by CLAUDE.md rule 11 (it is a design across crates). It touches `actions.ts` next to #3768's tap path, so it should be built after #3768 lands.
